notes: §1989:A.2.44.4 RV2: "The character string returned has the same length as argument-1." At 85 RenderStringValue takes its third case arm (the LOCALE phrase and the CHARACTER CLASSIFICATION clause that select the two locale arms are refused at 85 with COBOL0900) and calls CobolIntrinsics.UpperCase on the argument's whole image; its ToUpperInvariant is a simple case mapping, one character to one, so a letter whose full uppercase is two letters (the sharp s) stays one character. Probed at --std 85: a group, an OCCURS DEPENDING group at its current count, a reference-modified item, a nested function and non-ASCII letters each returned FUNCTION LENGTH equal to the argument's. The witness raises a PIC X item and displays the result's LENGTH and content.

next.reason: 1985: "The character string returned has the same length as argument-1."; 2023: "When the correspondence of lowercase and uppercase letters is not one-to-one, the character string returned may be longer or shorter". 1985 always returns a result as long as argument-1. 2023 keeps that only for one-to-one case mapping; otherwise the length may differ.
